objective: Goals G3 and G16 ask which proof steps cause work. Keeping the five products and both reports fixed, can a checked proof that learns an affine consequence and uses it in still-live branches beat the cheapest proof that derives its steps afresh when binary questions, local checks and citations are charged comparably?
status: Complete: The fixed pair costs 23 in a tree and with one optional single-premise affine implication. Training the prescribed implication requires at least 25 units in total, and the optimum with general guarded scalar learning is between 21 and 23.
title: Charged tree proofs and learned affine implications on five products
